questions.q: On a straight lane a reference point O is marked and rightward is taken as positive. A stall A is 30 m to the right of O and a stall B is 45 m to the left of O. A cyclist is at A at 10:00 am and at B at 10:02 am. Which description of her position is correct?
questions.a: Her position changed from +30 m to -45 m, so she was in motion with respect to O. Position has distance and direction; the sign shows which side of O she is on, and the reading changed, so she moved.
o: Her position changed from +30 m to -45 m, so she was in motion with respect to O
Her position changed only from 30 m to 45 m, because a position carries no sign
Her position did not change, because she was on the same lane both times
Her position changed from +30 m to +45 m, because distance is always positive

questions.q: A bench stands in a park. Ritu measures its position from the park gate and finds it unchanged for a whole week. Her teacher adds that the Earth moves around the Sun. Which statement is consistent with both observations?
questions.a: The bench is at rest with respect to the gate and the Earth's motion does not contradict this. Rest or motion is stated with respect to a chosen reference point; the bench is at rest for the gate and in motion for the Sun.
o: The bench is at rest with respect to the gate and the Earth's motion does not contradict this
The bench is not at rest because the Earth is moving, so Ritu's measurement is wrong
The bench is in motion with respect to the gate, because everything moves
The bench has no position, because a reference point must be the Sun

questions.q: A toy car's position from a reference point O on a straight table (right positive) was noted as +10 cm at 0 s, +25 cm at 2 s, +25 cm at 4 s and +40 cm at 6 s. In which interval was the car at rest with respect to O?
questions.a: Between 2 s and 4 s only. Position is unchanged (+25 cm) only between 2 s and 4 s; staying on one side of O does not mean staying put.
o: Between 2 s and 4 s only
Between 0 s and 2 s only
Between 4 s and 6 s only
Throughout the 6 s, since it stayed on the right of O

questions.q: On a football ground, Rahul takes the goal post G as the reference point, positive towards the centre spot C, and records a player 20 m from G towards C. Sana takes C as the reference point, positive towards G. The length GC is 50 m. Which pair of recorded positions for the same player is correct?
questions.a: Rahul records +20 m and Sana records +30 m. The player is 20 m from G on the C side; from C he is 50 - 20 = 30 m away on the G side, which Sana has taken as positive. Both records are valid because each fixed a reference point and a positive direction.
o: Rahul records +20 m and Sana records +30 m
Rahul records +20 m and Sana records -30 m
Rahul records +20 m and Sana records +20 m
Rahul records -20 m and Sana records +30 m

questions.q: Which statement about describing position on a straight line is false?
questions.a: An object that stays 25 m from the reference point for 10 s must be at rest. Direction also matters; an object can stay 25 m from O and still change position, for example by going from +25 m to -25 m.
o: An object that stays 25 m from the reference point for 10 s must be at rest
A reading of -25 m and a reading of +25 m are 25 m from the reference point on opposite sides
An object at the reference point itself has position 0 m
Two objects can have the same distance from O but different positions

questions.q: A drone flying along a straight line is read as -35 m from the reference point O at one instant and -20 m 5 s later (right positive). What does this show?
questions.a: It stayed on the left of O and moved 15 m towards O. Both readings are on the left of O, so the sign is unchanged; the reading changed from -35 to -20, which is a move of 15 m to the right, nearer to O.
o: It stayed on the left of O and moved 15 m towards O
It moved from the left of O to the right of O
It stayed at rest, because both readings are negative
It moved 15 m away from O on the left

questions.q:
A student studies how position is described on a straight line.
Statement 1: The distance of an object from the reference point alone is enough to describe its position.
Statement 2: An object whose reading changes from +15 m to -15 m has changed its position even though its distance from O is the same.
Statement 3: If the reading with respect to the reference point does not change with time, the object is at rest with respect to it.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 and 3 only. Statement 1 is false: the direction from the reference point must also be given. Statements 2 and 3 follow the definition of position, motion and rest.
o: 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
3 only
1 and 3 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A tree beside a road is at rest with respect to the road but in motion with respect to the Sun.
Reason (R): Whether an object is in motion or at rest depends on the reference point with respect to which its position is described.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. Both are true, and the second statement is exactly why the same tree can be both.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q: Rightward is positive. A runner stands 12 m to the left of O. If the class decides to take leftward as positive instead, her position is recorded as ___ m.

A cat sits 6 m to the right of a pole (the reference point, right positive) at 4:00 pm and 6 m to the left of it at 4:05 pm.
(a) Write the cat's two positions with their signs.
(b) By how much, and in which direction, has its position changed?
questions.a: (a) +6 m at 4:00 pm and -6 m at 4:05 pm. (b) The change is -6 - (+6) = -12 m, so the position changed by 12 m towards the left.
s: Part (a): +6 m and -6 m with signs
Part (b): change of 12 m towards the left, using the two positions

questions.q:
A scooter is parked at a school gate. A rider passes slowly along the road outside.
(a) With the gate as the reference point, is the scooter at rest or in motion?
(b) The rider uses himself as the reference point and says the scooter is 'moving backwards past him'. Why do the two descriptions not contradict each other?
questions.a: (a) At rest, since its position with respect to the gate does not change. (b) The rider's reference point is himself, and the scooter's position with respect to him keeps changing; motion and rest are always stated with respect to a chosen reference point.
s: Part (a): at rest with respect to the gate
Part (b): different reference points give different, equally valid descriptions

questions.q: True or False: An object recorded at -20 m on a straight line is closer to the reference point than an object recorded at +10 m. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. The object at -20 m is 20 m from the reference point, while the one at +10 m is only 10 m away.
s: Reason: the sign only gives the side of the reference point; the distance is 20 m against 10 m

questions.q: A student's wall clock reads 10:00:00 when a cyclist is at the pole and 10:00:30 when she is at the next pole. Using these two readings, differentiate an instant of time from a time interval.
questions.a: Each reading (10:00:00 or 10:00:30) is a single instant, one reading of the clock. The time interval is the duration between the two readings, here 30 s.
s: Each clock reading is an instant
The duration between two readings, 30 s, is the time interval

questions.q: Ishaan tells his friend, 'My house is 500 m from the school.' His friend says this does not fix where the house is. Do you agree? Name what is missing.
questions.a: Yes, I agree. The statement gives only a distance from a reference point (the school); the direction from the school (for example to its right or left, or east or west) is also needed to describe the position.
s: Names direction from the reference point as the missing item

questions.q: Neha claims: 'A bridge pillar stands still, so it is at rest and not in motion with respect to anything.' Test her claim.
questions.a: The claim is not correct. The pillar is at rest with respect to the river bank, since its position does not change. With respect to a boat passing under the bridge, the pillar's position changes with time, so it is in motion. Rest or motion depends on the reference point.
s: Rest with respect to the bank
Motion with respect to the boat, so it depends on the reference point

questions.q: Show that an object cannot be at rest with respect to a reference point O and also be at +20 m at one instant and -20 m at another.
questions.a: An object is at rest if its position with respect to O does not change with time. +20 m and -20 m are different positions, since they are on opposite sides of O. So the position has changed between the two instants and the object is in motion, not at rest.
s: Rest means no change of position
+20 m and -20 m are different positions
Conclusion: the object is in motion

questions.q: A trolley moves on a straight track with the lamp post O as reference point (right positive). Its positions are 4 m at 0 s, 12 m at 2 s, 12 m at 4 s, -6 m at 6 s and -6 m at 8 s. (i) In which intervals is it at rest? (ii) Between which two instants does it cross O? (iii) What is the change in position from 0 s to 8 s?
questions.a: (i) At rest from 2 s to 4 s and from 6 s to 8 s, since the position is unchanged. (ii) It crosses O between 4 s and 6 s, because the sign changes from +12 m to -6 m. (iii) -6 - 4 = -10 m, i.e. 10 m to the left.
s: Crosses O between 4 s and 6 s, with the sign-change reason
Net change -10 m (10 m to the left)

questions.q:
A runner on a straight lane is noted from a tree T taken as reference point (right positive): +10 m at 0 s, +30 m at 5 s, +30 m at 10 s, -20 m at 15 s, -20 m at 20 s and 0 m at 25 s.
(i) Find the change in position in each 5 s interval.
(ii) State the intervals in which she is at rest.
(iii) Between which instants does she cross T?
(iv) Is she at rest from 20 s to 25 s? Explain.
questions.a: (i) +20 m, 0 m, -50 m, 0 m, +20 m. (ii) 5-10 s and 15-20 s (no change in position). (iii) Between 10 s and 15 s, as the sign goes from + to -. (iv) No: her reading changed from -20 m at 20 s to 0 m at 25 s, so her position changed during the interval; rest requires the position to stay unchanged over time.
s: Crossing between 10 s and 15 s with reason
Not at rest from 20 s to 25 s; position changed by +20 m

questions.q:
A post office P and a temple T lie on a straight road with T 100 m to the right of P. A school is 30 m to the right of P. Asha takes P as the reference point with right positive. Bhavna takes T as the reference point with left positive. A cyclist is at the school at 0 s and 60 m to the right of P at 10 s.
(i) Write Asha's two positions of the cyclist.
(ii) Write Bhavna's two positions.
(iii) Find the change in position for each of them.
(iv) Do the girls disagree about whether the cyclist moved? Justify.
questions.a: (i) Asha: +30 m and +60 m. (ii) Bhavna: the school is 100 - 30 = 70 m left of T, so +70 m; the 60 m point is 40 m left of T, so +40 m. (iii) Asha: +30 m; Bhavna: -30 m. (iv) No. Their numbers and signs differ because of different reference points and positive directions, but both show the position changed by 30 m, so both agree the cyclist moved.
s: Justification: sign and values depend on the chosen reference and positive direction, but the change is 30 m for both

questions.q:
A mall in Pune has a basement level B1 that is 4 m below the ground floor and floors 1 to 5 that are each 4 m above the one below. The ground floor is taken as the reference point (0 m) with upward as positive. A lift runs from floor 3 to B1.
(a) Write the positions of floor 3 and of B1 with their signs.
(b) Find the change in position of the lift in going from floor 3 to B1, with direction.
(c) The manager considers instead taking the top floor (floor 5) as reference with downward as positive. Write the new positions of floor 3 and B1.
(d) The lift display should show a position for each floor. Which reference point would you choose, and what do you give up?
questions.a: (a) Floor 3: +12 m; B1: -4 m. (b) -4 - 12 = -16 m, i.e. 16 m downward. (c) Floor 3 is 8 m below the top: +8 m; B1 is 24 m below the top: +24 m. (d) Either is acceptable if justified: the ground reference gives natural signs (below ground is negative) but needs minus signs; the top-floor reference keeps every reading positive but the numbers for the basement become large and a reader must know the positive direction is downward.
s: Part (d): a choice supported by a trade-off in the data

questions.q:
Tarun sits in a train standing at Vijayawada station, with a second train on the next track. Looking only at the second train, he suddenly feels his own train is moving forward. He then looks at the platform pillar near his window: it has stayed opposite the same window for the last minute. The second train is seen sliding slowly backwards past the window.
(a) With which reference point did Tarun feel that his own train was moving?
(b) What does the unchanging pillar position tell him about his own train, and with respect to what?
(c) With the platform as the reference point, is the second train at rest or in motion? Why?
(d) To check his own train's state, Tarun can trust either the pillar or the second train. Which should he trust, and what limitation does your choice have?
questions.a: (a) The second train, taken as the reference point. (b) The pillar's position with respect to him does not change, so his train is at rest with respect to the platform. (c) In motion: its position with respect to the platform changes with time as it slides backwards. (d) The pillar is the better choice because it is fixed to the platform, so it does not itself move; the limitation is that it gives rest or motion only with respect to the platform and needs a clear view of it, whereas the other train may itself be moving.
s: Part (a): the second train as reference point
Part (b): at rest with respect to the platform
Part (c): in motion, since its position with respect to the platform changes
Part (d): chooses the pillar and states the limitation

questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically up from a point O on a terrace and rises 80 cm to its highest point B. It then falls and is caught at a point C that is 30 cm above O. Taking up as positive, which pair is correct for the whole motion from O to C?
questions.a: Distance travelled 130 cm; displacement 30 cm upward. The path is 80 cm up and then 80 - 30 = 50 cm down, a total of 130 cm; the net change in position is from O to C, 30 cm upward.
o: Distance travelled 130 cm; displacement 30 cm upward
Distance travelled 30 cm; displacement 130 cm upward
Distance travelled 110 cm; displacement 50 cm upward
Distance travelled 130 cm; displacement 130 cm upward

questions.q: An auto-rickshaw leaves a house, goes 6 km to a bank and returns to the same house. The driver's fuel bill for the trip depends on which quantity, and what is its value?
questions.a: The total distance travelled, 12 km. Fuel is used up along the whole path, so it depends on the distance travelled (6 + 6 = 12 km); the displacement is 0 because the trip ends at the start.
o: The total distance travelled, 12 km
The displacement, 12 km
The displacement, 0 km
The total distance travelled, 6 km

questions.q: On a straight lane, jogger P walks directly from the gate to a bench 150 m away. Jogger Q walks 200 m past the gate in the same direction and then comes back 50 m to the same bench. Which comparison is correct?
questions.a: Their displacements are equal but Q has travelled 100 m more distance. Both change position by 150 m from the gate to the bench, so the displacements are equal; the distances are 150 m and 200 + 50 = 250 m, a difference of 100 m.
o: Their displacements are equal but Q has travelled 100 m more distance
Their distances are equal because both finish at the bench
Q has the larger displacement because Q walked more
P has the larger displacement because P walked in a straight line

questions.q: A bus goes 15 km east to a town and then 6 km west to a village on the same straight road. Rekha says its displacement is 21 km. What is her slip, and what is the correct displacement?
questions.a: She added the lengths, which gives distance; displacement is 15 - 6 = 9 km east. Adding path lengths gives the distance travelled (21 km); displacement is the net change in position, 9 km towards the east.
o: She added the lengths, which gives distance; displacement is 15 - 6 = 9 km east
She forgot the direction; the displacement is 21 km west
She should have subtracted the lengths for distance; distance is 9 km
She is correct, because displacement is the total path length

questions.q: Which of the following can never be true for an object moving along a straight line?
questions.a: The magnitude of its displacement is more than the distance it travelled. The magnitude of displacement is less than or equal to the distance travelled, never more.
o: The magnitude of its displacement is more than the distance it travelled
Its displacement is zero but the distance it travelled is not zero
Its displacement is equal in magnitude to the distance it travelled
The distance it travelled is more than the magnitude of its displacement

questions.q:
Read these statements about an athlete on a straight track.
Statement 1: An athlete who runs 100 m forward and then 100 m back has a distance travelled of 200 m and a displacement of 0 m.
Statement 2: When the path is curved, the magnitude of displacement can be greater than the distance travelled.
Statement 3: The direction of displacement is from the position at the first instant towards the position at the second instant.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 3 only. Statement 2 is false because the magnitude of displacement is never greater than the distance travelled. Statements 1 and 3 are correct.
o: 1 and 3 only
3 only
1 and 2 only
2 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A boy who walks 8 m east and then 8 m west has travelled a distance of zero because he is back where he started.
Reason (R): Displacement is the net change in position of an object between two given instants of time.
questions.a: A is false but R is true. A is false: the distance is 16 m, the whole path covered. R is true, and it is the reason the displacement, not the distance, is zero.
o: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.q: A robot moves 120 m east, then 45 m west, then 20 m east along one straight line. The magnitude of its displacement is ___ m.

Match each walk along a straight line (column I) with its distance and displacement magnitude (column II).
Column I: 1. A drone flies 40 m north and then 40 m back south  2. A cyclist rides 75 m east without turning back  3. A child climbs 12 m up a ladder and comes down 5 m  4. A runner runs 90 m forward and 35 m back
Column II: a. distance 75 m, displacement 75 m  b. distance 80 m, displacement 0 m  c. distance 17 m, displacement 7 m  d. distance 125 m, displacement 55 m
questions.a: 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d. Distance adds the path lengths; displacement is the net change: 40 - 40 = 0, 75, 12 - 5 = 7 and 90 - 35 = 55.

questions.q:
A student walks from one end of a straight 50 m corridor to the other end and back, and does this twice in all.
(a) Find the distance she has travelled.
(b) Find her displacement, and say why it is different from your answer to (a).
questions.a: (a) 4 x 50 = 200 m. (b) 0 m, because she ends at her starting end; the displacement is only the net change in position, while the distance counts all the path covered.
s: Part (b): 0 m with the reason that displacement is the net change

questions.q:
A ball is thrown straight up from the ground (origin O, up positive) and rises 20 m.
(a) State its distance travelled and displacement when it is at the top.
(b) State both when it is caught back at O, and explain why one of them stopped growing while the other kept growing.
questions.a: (a) Distance 20 m, displacement 20 m upward. (b) Distance 40 m, displacement 0 m. On the way down the path length keeps adding, but the net change in position from O shrinks back to zero.
s: Part (b): 40 m and 0 m with the reason

questions.q: True or False: If the displacement of an object between two instants is zero, the object cannot have moved at all during that interval. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. A zero displacement only means it was at the same position at the two instants; it may have travelled a large distance and returned.
s: Reason: displacement is the net change in position; a return trip gives displacement 0 but a non-zero distance such as 16 m for 8 m out and back

questions.q: A plumber says, 'I went 3 km today.' A courier says, 'I went 3 km towards the market.' Which statement gives a distance and which gives a displacement? What makes the difference?
questions.a: The plumber's statement gives a distance (a numerical value only) and the courier's gives a displacement (value with direction, towards the market). Displacement needs a direction as well as a magnitude, distance does not.

questions.q: Ranjit says, 'The magnitude of displacement is always smaller than the distance travelled.' Is he right? State the exact relation and when the two are equal.
questions.a: Not exactly right. The magnitude of displacement is less than or equal to the distance travelled; they are equal when the object moves in one direction without turning back.
s: Correct relation: less than or equal
Equality when there is no turn back in a straight line

questions.q: Mehul claims: 'On a straight track, if an object turns back once after moving forward, the distance it travels is greater than the magnitude of its displacement.' Test the claim with an example of 70 m forward and 20 m back.
questions.a: The claim is correct. Distance = 70 + 20 = 90 m, displacement = 70 - 20 = 50 m in the forward direction, and 90 m is more than 50 m. Whenever part of the path is retraced, that part adds to the distance but subtracts from the displacement.
s: Reason: retraced part adds to distance but cancels displacement

questions.q: Write a movement of a toy car along a straight line, with its numbers, for which the distance travelled is 60 m and the magnitude of displacement is 20 m. Show that your numbers work.
questions.a: Example: it moves 40 m forward and then 20 m back. Distance = 40 + 20 = 60 m; displacement = 40 - 20 = 20 m forward. (If x is forward and y is back, x + y = 60 and x - y = 20 give x = 40 and y = 20.)
s: A movement with a turn back

questions.q: A student goes up in a school building from the ground floor to the 5th floor and then walks down to the 3rd floor. Each floor is 3.5 m high. Find (i) the total vertical distance travelled, (ii) the displacement from the starting point, with direction, and (iii) say which of these decides how tired she feels.
questions.a: (i) Up 5 x 3.5 = 17.5 m, down 2 x 3.5 = 7 m, total 24.5 m. (ii) 17.5 - 7 = 10.5 m upward. (iii) The distance travelled, since effort depends on the whole path, not only the net change.
s: Distance decides tiredness, with a reason

questions.q:
A cleaning robot moves along a straight corridor from its charging point O (east positive) in five moves: 12 m east, 5 m west, 8 m east, 20 m west and 3 m east.
(i) Find its position after each move.
(ii) Find the total distance travelled.
(iii) Find its final displacement.
(iv) After which move does it cross O?
(v) Compare the distance and the magnitude of the final displacement and say why they differ.
questions.a: (i) +12, +7, +15, -5, -2 m. (ii) 12 + 5 + 8 + 20 + 3 = 48 m. (iii) 2 m west. (iv) After the fourth move, because the position changes from +15 m to -5 m. (v) 48 m is much greater than 2 m because the robot kept reversing, so most of its path was retraced.
s: Crosses O during the fourth move

questions.q:
Kiran lives 180 m from a post box on a straight road. He walks to the post box, finds that he forgot the letter, walks back home, collects it, walks to the post box again, posts it, and then walks on 70 m beyond it to a bank in the same direction.
(i) Find the total distance he travelled.
(ii) Find his displacement from home.
(iii) If he walks at a steady pace, which quantity gives the time he spends walking? Explain.
(iv) Which quantity tells where the bank is with respect to home?
(v) Could his displacement ever exceed 610 m on this walk? Justify.
questions.a: (i) 180 + 180 + 180 + 70 = 610 m. (ii) 180 + 70 = 250 m in the direction of the bank. (iii) The distance, 610 m, because time at a steady pace depends on the whole path walked. (iv) The displacement, 250 m in that direction. (v) No: the magnitude of displacement is never more than the distance travelled, 610 m.
s: Displacement 250 m in the direction of the bank
Time depends on distance, with reason

questions.q:
A delivery rider's warehouse W is at 0 m on a straight road (east positive). Three customers live at D1 = -600 m (west of W), D2 = +1000 m and D3 = +300 m. Route A is W to D1 to D2 to D3 and back to W. Route B is W to D2 to D1 to D3 and back to W. The bike's running cost is Rs 2.5 per km. The parcel for D2 is ice cream that melts quickly.
(a) Find the total distance of Route A.
(b) Find the displacement of the rider for the whole of Route A.
(c) Find the total distance of Route B and its extra running cost over Route A.
(d) How far does the ice cream travel before delivery on each route? Which route would you choose, and what do you give up?
questions.a: (a) 600 + 1600 + 700 + 300 = 3200 m. (b) 0 m, since the rider returns to W. (c) 1000 + 1600 + 900 + 300 = 3800 m; extra = 600 m = 0.6 km x Rs 2.5 = Rs 1.50. (d) On Route A the ice cream travels 600 + 1600 = 2200 m before delivery; on Route B only 1000 m. Either route is acceptable if justified: Route B delivers the ice cream 1200 m sooner but costs Rs 1.50 more; Route A saves Rs 1.50 but the ice cream travels 2200 m before it is delivered.
s: Part (d): 2200 m versus 1000 m, and a choice with the trade-off named

questions.q:
A physics club throws a ball straight up from a point O at hand level and records readings (up positive): at A, 50 cm above O on the way up; at B, 100 cm above O (the highest point); at C, 50 cm above O on the way down; at O again; and at D, 30 cm below O, where the ball lands in a basket. The ball travels only along the vertical line.
(a) Find the distance travelled and the displacement when the ball is at B.
(b) Find both when the ball is back at O.
(c) Find both when it reaches D, with direction.
(d) To report how high the ball rose above the hand, a student suggests quoting the distance at D. Is that a good choice? Name the reading you would use and justify.
questions.a: (a) Distance 100 cm; displacement 100 cm upward. (b) Distance 200 cm; displacement 0 cm. (c) Distance 100 + 100 + 30 = 230 cm; displacement 30 cm downward. (d) No: the distance at D includes the fall below O. The displacement at B (100 cm upward) gives the height reached, because it is the largest reading above O; the distance at B also gives 100 cm only because the ball had not turned back.
s: Part (d): rejects distance at D and justifies the reading at B

questions.q: A cyclist rides 12 km north in 40 minutes and then 12 km back south along the same road in 20 minutes. Which row gives her average speed and average velocity for the whole trip?
questions.a: Average speed 24 km/h; average velocity 0 km/h. Total distance 24 km in 1 h gives 24 km/h; she ends where she started, so the displacement and average velocity are zero.
o: Average speed 24 km/h; average velocity 0 km/h
Average speed 0 km/h; average velocity 24 km/h
Average speed 12 km/h; average velocity 12 km/h north
Average speed 24 km/h; average velocity 24 km/h south

questions.q: Priya must find the time a scooter at a steady 54 km/h takes to cover 600 m. She divides 600 by 54 and gets 11.1 s. What is the slip, and what is the right answer?
questions.a: The units do not match; 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so the time is 40 s. 600 m is in metres but 54 is in km/h; 54 x 1000 / 3600 = 15 m/s, and 600 / 15 = 40 s.
o: The units do not match; 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so the time is 40 s
The formula is wrong; time = speed x distance = 32400 s
She should have used 54 m/s, giving 11.1 s as correct
The scooter's velocity is needed, not its speed, so no answer exists

questions.q: A toy car covers 4 m, 6 m, 8 m and 10 m in four successive seconds along a straight line. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The motion is non-uniform, and its average speed over the 4 s is 7 m/s. Unequal distances in equal times mean non-uniform motion; the average speed is the total distance 28 m divided by 4 s, which is 7 m/s, not the last second's 10 m/s.
o: The motion is non-uniform, and its average speed over the 4 s is 7 m/s
The motion is uniform, and its average speed over the 4 s is 10 m/s
The motion is non-uniform, and its average speed over the 4 s is 10 m/s
The motion is uniform, and its average speed over the 4 s is 7 m/s

questions.q: A train covers its first 120 km at 60 km/h and the next 120 km, in the same direction, at 120 km/h. Hari says its average speed is (60 + 120)/2 = 90 km/h. What is the true average speed?
questions.a: 80 km/h, because the total time is 2 h + 1 h. Average speed is total distance over total time: 240 km in 2 h + 1 h = 3 h gives 80 km/h; the two halves take unequal times, so the simple mean of speeds is wrong.
o: 80 km/h, because the total time is 2 h + 1 h
90 km/h, because speeds are always averaged
100 km/h, because the faster half dominates
60 km/h, because the slower half sets the pace

questions.q: For motion along a straight line, which of the following quantities can take a negative value?
questions.a: Average velocity. Average velocity carries the sign of the displacement; speed, distance and time interval are never negative.
o: Average velocity
Average speed
Distance travelled
Time interval

questions.q:
Read these statements about a round trip made by a car.
Statement 1: The car's average speed can be non-zero while its average velocity is zero.
Statement 2: If the average velocity over an interval is zero, the object must have stayed at rest throughout the interval.
Statement 3: Average speed is given a negative sign when the car moves backwards.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 only. Statement 1 is correct (a round trip). Statement 2 is false because a zero displacement can follow a long path. Statement 3 is false because average speed uses distance and has no direction.
o: 1 only
3 only
2 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A car moving along a straight road at a constant 60 km/h without ever turning back has an average speed equal to the magnitude of its average velocity.
Reason (R): The SI unit of average speed and of average velocity is the same, metre per second.
questions.a: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A. Both statements are true, but equal units do not cause the equality; it holds because the displacement equals the distance when there is no turn back.
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q: A bus covers 108 km in 1.5 h in one direction. Its average speed in metres per second is ___ m/s.

Match each trip (column I) with its average speed and the magnitude of its average velocity (column II).
Column I: 1. A girl swims 50 m along a pool and 50 m back in 100 s  2. A car drives 120 km in one direction in 2 h  3. A bus goes 60 km east in 1 h and 60 km west in the next 1 h  4. A jogger runs 300 m east in 100 s
Column II: a. speed 60 km/h, velocity magnitude 60 km/h  b. speed 1 m/s, velocity magnitude 0 m/s  c. speed 3 m/s, velocity magnitude 3 m/s  d. speed 60 km/h, velocity magnitude 0 km/h
questions.a: 1-b, 2-a, 3-d, 4-c. Speed is total distance over time; velocity uses the displacement, which is 0 for the two round trips and equals the distance for the two one-way trips.

questions.q:
A van travels 90 km north in 2 h and then 30 km south in 1 h on a straight road.
(a) Find its average speed for the 3 h.
(b) Find its average velocity, with direction.
questions.a: (a) (90 + 30) km / 3 h = 40 km/h. (b) Displacement = 90 - 30 = 60 km north; average velocity = 60 / 3 = 20 km/h north.

questions.q:
A skater covers 3 m, 5 m and 7 m in three successive seconds along a straight line.
(a) Is this uniform motion? Give the reason.
(b) Find her average speed for the 3 s and say whether it equals her speed in the first second.
questions.a: (a) No: she covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, so the motion is non-uniform (speed increasing). (b) (3 + 5 + 7)/3 = 5 m/s, which is not equal to 3 m/s in the first second.
s: Part (a): non-uniform, unequal distances in equal times
Part (b): 5 m/s, different from the first second's 3 m/s

questions.q: True or False: Over any time interval, the average speed of an object can never be smaller than the magnitude of its average velocity. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Average speed uses the distance travelled and the magnitude of average velocity uses the displacement, and the magnitude of displacement is never more than the distance travelled, for the same time interval.
s: Reason: distance is at least as large as the magnitude of displacement, and both are divided by the same time

questions.q: Average velocity is called the average rate of change of position. A car is at 20 m from the reference point at 2 s and at 80 m at 5 s on a straight road. Use the rate of change idea to find its average velocity, and say what the sign shows.
questions.a: Change in position = 80 - 20 = 60 m in a time interval of 5 - 2 = 3 s, so the average velocity is 60/3 = 20 m/s. The positive sign shows that the displacement, and so the velocity, is in the positive direction.
s: 20 m/s from change in position over time interval
Positive sign means the positive direction

questions.q: Neeraj says, 'Two cars with the same average speed over a trip must also have the same average velocity.' Do you agree? Support your answer with a short example.
questions.a: No. Average velocity depends on displacement. One car going 60 km in 1 h in a straight line has speed and velocity 60 km/h, while another going 30 km out and 30 km back in 1 h has the same average speed of 60 km/h but an average velocity of 0.
s: Disagrees, with displacement as the deciding quantity
A correct example of equal speeds and different velocities

questions.q: Imran claims: 'For any journey along a straight line, the average speed equals the magnitude of the average velocity.' Is he right? Test it with the swimmer who swims 25 m to the far end of a pool and 25 m back in 50 s.
questions.a: He is partly right. When the swimmer goes one way only, distance equals displacement and the two are equal. In the 50 s trip the average speed is 50/50 = 1 m/s but the average velocity is 0/50 = 0, so the claim fails when the direction reverses.
s: Fails for the 50 s trip: 1 m/s against 0 m/s

questions.q: A cyclist covers the first 18 km of a ride at 12 km/h and the next 6 km at 6 km/h. Her friend says the average speed is the mean of the two speeds, 9 km/h. (i) Find the time taken for each part. (ii) Find the average speed for the whole ride. (iii) Is the friend right?
questions.a: (i) 18/12 = 1.5 h and 6/6 = 1 h. (ii) Total distance 24 km in 2.5 h gives 24/2.5 = 9.6 km/h. (iii) No: average speed is total distance divided by total time (9.6 km/h), not the mean of the two speeds (9 km/h), because the time spent at each speed is different.
s: Friend is wrong; total distance over total time, unequal times

questions.q: A dog runs for 20 s on a straight lane and its average speed is 6 m/s while its average velocity is zero. Describe a possible run with distances, and show that the numbers fit.
questions.a: Example: it runs 60 m away in 10 s and 60 m back in the next 10 s. Total distance 120 m in 20 s gives 120/20 = 6 m/s; it ends where it started, so displacement and average velocity are zero.
s: A run that returns to the start

questions.q:
Bus A goes from city P towards city Q, 180 km east, non-stop in 3 h. Bus B leaves P with it, goes 150 km east in 2 h and then, because of a diversion, 30 km west in 1 h.
(i) Find the average speed of A.
(ii) Find the average speed of B for the 3 h.
(iii) Find the average velocity of each, with direction.
(iv) A passenger says both buses made equal progress towards Q because their average speeds are equal. Evaluate the statement.
questions.a: (i) 180/3 = 60 km/h. (ii) (150 + 30)/3 = 60 km/h. (iii) A: 180/3 = 60 km/h east. B: displacement 150 - 30 = 120 km east, so 120/3 = 40 km/h east. (iv) Not correct: equal average speeds only show equal distances covered along the paths. Progress towards Q is the displacement; A is 180 km east of P and B only 120 km, so A made more progress.
s: Velocities 60 km/h east and 40 km/h east
Reason: progress is measured by displacement (180 km against 120 km)

questions.q:
A cyclist rides on a straight road at 6 m/s for 50 s, rests for 30 s, then rides on in the same direction at 10 m/s for 20 s.
(i) Find the distance covered in each of the three stages.
(ii) Find the total distance and the total time.
(iii) Find the average speed for the whole journey.
(iv) Priya says the average speed is (6 + 0 + 10)/3 m/s. Compare with your answer and give the reason for the difference.
(v) Is the magnitude of her average velocity equal to the average speed? Why?
questions.a: (i) 300 m, 0 m and 200 m. (ii) 500 m in 100 s. (iii) 500/100 = 5 m/s. (iv) Priya's value is about 5.33 m/s, which is wrong because the three stages last different times; average speed is total distance over total time. (v) Yes, 5 m/s, because she moves in one direction only, so displacement equals distance.
s: Priya's 5.33 m/s is wrong because the stages last unequal times
Equal, since there is no turn back

questions.q:
Ranjani trains on a straight park path with a gate G at one end. She runs 400 m from G to a fountain F in 100 s, rests at F for 40 s, and then walks back 300 m towards G to a bench in 150 s. A fitness app can report either her average speed or her average velocity for a session, and her coach wants one number to track her effort.
(a) Find her average speed while running from G to F.
(b) Find her average speed for the whole 290 s session.
(c) Find her average velocity for the whole session, with direction.
(d) Which number should the coach track, and what does that choice hide?
questions.a: (a) 400/100 = 4 m/s. (b) (400 + 300)/290 = 700/290, about 2.41 m/s. (c) Displacement = 400 - 300 = 100 m from G towards F, so 100/290, about 0.34 m/s towards F. (d) Average speed is the better measure of effort because it counts all the path covered (700 m); it hides how the time was spent (the rest and the walk). Average velocity, 0.34 m/s, would suggest very little work and hides the back-and-forth.
s: Part (c): about 0.34 m/s towards the fountain
Part (d): chooses average speed and names what is hidden

questions.q:
A school bus leaves the depot at 7:00 am, travels 12 km to a stop in 20 minutes, halts there for 10 minutes, and then travels 18 km further in the same direction in 30 minutes to reach the school at 8:00 am.
(a) Find the bus's speed during each of the two moving legs in km/h.
(b) Find its average speed for the whole hour.
(c) Find its average velocity for the hour and say why it equals the average speed.
(d) The principal wants the bus to reach the school at 7:50 am. Option 1: keep the 10 minute halt and drive faster. Option 2: remove the halt and keep the earlier speed. Work out what each needs and say which you prefer.
questions.a: (a) 12 km in 1/3 h = 36 km/h; 18 km in 0.5 h = 36 km/h. (b) 30 km in 1 h = 30 km/h. (c) 30 km/h in the direction of the school, equal to the average speed because the bus never turns back, so displacement equals distance. (d) Keeping the halt needs 30 km in 40 minutes of moving time: 30 / (2/3) = 45 km/h. Removing the halt needs 30 km in 50 minutes: 36 km/h, the same speed as before. A reasoned choice is accepted: removing the halt keeps the safe speed but children at the stop lose their pick-up time; keeping the halt keeps the pick-up but needs a much higher speed.
s: Part (c): 30 km/h towards the school, no turn back
Part (d): 45 km/h and 36 km/h with a justified choice

questions.q: A car on a straight road speeds up from 36 km/h to 72 km/h in 5 s. Aman writes its average acceleration as (72 - 36)/5 = 7.2 m/s^2. What is the correct value and the slip?
questions.a: 2 m/s^2; the speeds were not converted to m/s (10 m/s and 20 m/s). In m/s the speeds are 10 and 20, so the average acceleration is (20 - 10)/5 = 2 m/s^2; km/h and s do not give m/s^2.
o: 2 m/s^2; the speeds were not converted to m/s (10 m/s and 20 m/s)
7.2 m/s^2; the answer is right because km/h can be used with seconds
20 m/s^2; the time should have been multiplied
0.5 m/s^2; the time interval should have been squared

questions.q: A bike moving at 18 m/s slows to 6 m/s in 4 s. Taking its direction of motion as positive, which statement is correct?
questions.a: Its average acceleration is -3 m/s^2, opposite to its velocity. (6 - 18)/4 = -3 m/s^2; the speed is decreasing, so the acceleration is opposite to the velocity.
o: Its average acceleration is -3 m/s^2, opposite to its velocity
Its average acceleration is +3 m/s^2, along its velocity
Its average acceleration is -12 m/s^2, along its velocity
Its average acceleration is +4.5 m/s^2, opposite to its velocity

questions.q: A stone is dropped from a tall building. Neglecting air, its velocity is 19.6 m/s downward after 2 s. With the downward direction positive, what is its velocity after 5 s?
questions.a: 49.0 m/s. The acceleration is constant at 9.8 m/s^2, so v = 0 + 9.8 x 5 = 49.0 m/s; 39.2 m/s is the value at 4 s and 29.4 m/s the value at 3 s.

questions.q: A train moves on a straight track at a steady 90 km/h for 10 minutes. Four students give its acceleration. Which one is right?
questions.a: Zero, because its velocity is not changing. Acceleration depends on how quickly velocity changes, not how large it is; here there is no change, so it is zero.
o: Zero, because its velocity is not changing
25 m/s^2, because its velocity is 25 m/s
Large, because 90 km/h is a high speed
Small but not zero, because it is a heavy train

questions.q: In which situation is the average acceleration of the object zero over the stated interval?
questions.a: A bus holds 15 m/s on a straight highway for 20 s. Only the bus has no change in velocity; each of the other three has velocity changing by equal amounts in equal time.
o: A bus holds 15 m/s on a straight highway for 20 s
A car slows from 20 m/s to 10 m/s in 5 s
A stone is dropped and falls for 3 s
A scooter speeds up from 5 m/s to 15 m/s in 5 s

questions.q:
A teacher writes three statements about acceleration on the board.
Statement 1: A bus moving at a constant velocity has zero acceleration even if its velocity is high.
Statement 2: If the magnitude of an object's velocity is decreasing, its average acceleration acts opposite to the direction of velocity.
Statement 3: For a freely falling object near the Earth's surface, the velocity increases by the same amount in every successive second.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 1, 2 and 3. All three follow the chapter: acceleration measures change of velocity, its direction rule for slowing down, and constant g = 9.8 m/s^2 for free fall.
o: 1, 2 and 3
3 only
2 and 3 only
1 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A car slowing from 20 m/s to 10 m/s in 5 s has an average acceleration of magnitude 2 m/s^2.
Reason (R): Average acceleration is the change in speed multiplied by the time interval.
questions.a: A is true but R is false. A is true: (20 - 10)/5 = 2. R is false because average acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time interval, not multiplied.
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true

questions.q: A cyclist slows from 8 m/s to 2 m/s in 3 s. Taking her direction of motion as positive, her average acceleration is ___ m/s^2.

Match each motion (column I) with its average acceleration (column II).
Column I: 1. A car starts from rest and reaches 20 m/s in 8 s  2. A train slows from 30 m/s to rest in 60 s  3. A ball in free fall near the Earth's surface  4. A scooter at a steady 40 km/h on a straight road for 5 minutes
Column II: a. 2.5 m/s^2 along the motion  b. 0.5 m/s^2 opposite to the motion  c. 9.8 m/s^2 along the motion, downward  d. zero
questions.a: 1-a, 2-b, 3-c, 4-d. (20 - 0)/8 = 2.5 along the motion; (0 - 30)/60 = -0.5, opposite to the motion; free fall has g; a steady velocity means no acceleration.

questions.q:
A motorbike speeds up from 6 m/s to 21 m/s in 5 s along a straight road.
(a) Find its average acceleration.
(b) If this acceleration stays constant, find its velocity 4 s later.
questions.a: (a) (21 - 6)/5 = 3 m/s^2. (b) The velocity rises by 3 x 4 = 12 m/s, so it is 21 + 12 = 33 m/s.
s: Part (b): 33 m/s using the constant acceleration from (a)

questions.q:
A car brakes from 25 m/s to 5 m/s in 4 s along a straight road.
(a) Find its average acceleration with sign, taking its direction of motion as positive.
(b) If the same acceleration continues, how much longer does it take to stop?
questions.a: (a) (5 - 25)/4 = -5 m/s^2. (b) Speed falls by 5 m/s every second, so the remaining 5 m/s is lost in 1 s.
s: Part (b): 1 s using the acceleration from (a)

questions.q: True or False: A ball dropped from rest has a velocity of 19.6 m/s after 2 s, so after 4 s its velocity is 39.2 m/s. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. Free fall has a constant acceleration g = 9.8 m/s^2, so the velocity grows by 9.8 m/s every second: 9.8 x 4 = 39.2 m/s.
s: Reason: the acceleration is constant at about 9.8 m/s^2, so velocity is proportional to time from rest

questions.q: A bus runs at a steady 20 m/s and then brakes to 8 m/s in 4 s. Say what its acceleration is in the steady part, and what it is in the braking part with its direction.
questions.a: Steady part: zero, because velocity is not changing. Braking part: (8 - 20)/4 = -3 m/s^2, i.e. 3 m/s^2 opposite to the direction of velocity.
s: 3 m/s^2 opposite to the velocity during braking

questions.q: For a car that brakes from 15 m/s to rest in 5 s, Kiran writes the acceleration as 3 m/s^2 and Lata writes -3 m/s^2. Can both be correct? Explain.
questions.a: Yes, if they chose different positive directions. Lata took the car's direction of motion as positive, so the slowing acceleration is negative. Kiran must have taken the opposite direction as positive; the magnitude is 3 m/s^2 either way, and the positive direction must not change within one problem.
s: Both can be right, depending on the positive direction
Magnitude 3 m/s^2 and direction opposite to velocity in both

questions.q: Meena claims: 'The speedometer of the car shows 90 km/h on a straight highway at constant velocity, so its acceleration must be large.' Test her claim.
questions.a: The claim is not correct. Acceleration is the change of velocity divided by the time interval. At constant velocity the change is zero, so the acceleration is zero however high the 90 km/h reading is.
s: Acceleration depends on change of velocity

questions.q: A skater has an initial velocity of 10 m/s and a constant acceleration of 2 m/s^2 in the same direction as her velocity. Show that she cannot have a velocity of 8 m/s after 3 s.
questions.a: The acceleration is in the direction of velocity, so her speed increases. After 3 s the velocity is 10 + 2 x 3 = 16 m/s. A value of 8 m/s would be a decrease, which needs an acceleration opposite to the velocity.
s: Acceleration along velocity means speed increases
8 m/s would need a decrease, so it is impossible

questions.q: A truck at 72 km/h slows to 36 km/h in 25 s on a straight road. (i) Find its average acceleration in m/s^2. (ii) State its direction relative to the velocity. (iii) If this acceleration stays constant, find its velocity 10 s after that (35 s after it began slowing).
questions.a: (i) 72 km/h = 20 m/s and 36 km/h = 10 m/s, so a = (10 - 20)/25 = -0.4 m/s^2. (ii) Opposite to the velocity, as the speed decreases. (iii) 10 + (-0.4)(10) = 6 m/s.

questions.q:
Two test cars X and Y move in a straight line. Their velocities (m/s) at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20 s are: X: 4, 10, 16, 22, 28 and Y: 4, 10, 18, 24, 28.
(i) Find X's average acceleration in each 5 s interval.
(ii) Find Y's average acceleration in each 5 s interval.
(iii) Which car has constant acceleration? Give the reason.
(iv) Find X's velocity at 30 s if its acceleration continues.
(v) Find each car's average acceleration over the whole 20 s and say what this shows about using only the whole-interval value.
questions.a: (i) 1.2 m/s^2 in every interval. (ii) 1.2, 1.6, 1.2 and 0.8 m/s^2. (iii) Car X: its velocity changes by equal amounts in equal intervals. (iv) 28 + 1.2 x 10 = 40 m/s. (v) Both are (28 - 4)/20 = 1.2 m/s^2, so equal whole-interval values do not show that the acceleration was constant; the smaller intervals must be checked.
s: Both 1.2 m/s^2 over 20 s; the whole-interval value hides the change in Y

questions.q:
A bus on a long straight highway moves at 18 km/h. The driver presses the accelerator for 8 s and the speed becomes 54 km/h. Later the driver brakes and the bus stops in 6 s.
(i) Find the average acceleration while the accelerator is pressed.
(ii) Find the average acceleration while braking.
(iii) State each direction relative to the velocity with the reason.
(iv) By what factor is the braking acceleration larger in magnitude?
(v) How long would the bus take to stop if its braking acceleration had the same magnitude as in (i)?
questions.a: (i) 18 km/h = 5 m/s and 54 km/h = 15 m/s, so a = (15 - 5)/8 = 1.25 m/s^2. (ii) (0 - 15)/6 = -2.5 m/s^2. (iii) First along the velocity because speed increases; second opposite to the velocity because speed decreases. (iv) 2.5/1.25 = 2 times. (v) 15/1.25 = 12 s.

questions.q:
A science club drops a ball from a high balcony. A camera shows the ball falling straight down and the club ignores air. They record its motion with the release point as the origin and the downward direction as positive. A member suggests that taking upward as positive would be more natural.
(a) Find the velocity of the ball 2.5 s after release.
(b) After how much time does its velocity reach 34.3 m/s?
(c) If upward were taken as positive, what would be the acceleration and the velocity at 2.5 s?
(d) Which positive direction should the club choose for its record, and what does the other choice cost?
questions.a: (a) 9.8 x 2.5 = 24.5 m/s downward. (b) 34.3 / 9.8 = 3.5 s. (c) The acceleration would be -9.8 m/s^2 and the velocity -24.5 m/s. (d) Either is acceptable if kept the same throughout: downward positive makes the falling readings positive but heights above the release point then become negative; upward positive suits heights but makes the velocity and acceleration negative.
s: Part (d): a choice with the cost of the other

questions.q:
A metro train leaves a station, speeds up from rest to 18 m/s in 20 s, then runs at 18 m/s for 100 s, and finally brakes to rest in 15 s. The operator can make the braking time shorter to save time at each station.
(a) Find the average acceleration in the speeding-up stage.
(b) Find the average acceleration while braking, with its direction.
(c) What is the acceleration during the 100 s run at 18 m/s? Why is it not large though the speed is high?
(d) If braking takes 10 s instead of 15 s, how many times larger is the braking acceleration, and would you accept this change given that standing passengers feel jolts?
questions.a: (a) 18/20 = 0.9 m/s^2. (b) (0 - 18)/15 = -1.2 m/s^2, opposite to the velocity. (c) Zero, because velocity is constant; acceleration depends on the change in velocity, not on how large it is. (d) 18/10 = 1.8 m/s^2, which is 1.8/1.2 = 1.5 times larger. A reasoned choice is accepted: it saves 5 s at each stop but passengers feel a stronger jolt (1.8 against 1.2 m/s^2).
s: Part (d): 1.5 times and a justified decision

questions.q: A position-time graph for object P is a straight line through the origin and the point (4 s, 48 m). The graph for object Q is a straight line through the origin and the point (6 s, 48 m), drawn on the same axes. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: P's line is steeper and P's velocity is 12 m/s, against 8 m/s for Q. Velocity is the slope: 48/4 = 12 m/s for P and 48/6 = 8 m/s for Q; the steeper line shows the larger velocity.
o: P's line is steeper and P's velocity is 12 m/s, against 8 m/s for Q
Q's line is steeper because Q takes longer, and its velocity is 8 m/s
Both lines have the same slope because both reach 48 m
P's velocity is 4 m/s and Q's is 6 m/s, read from the time values

questions.q: A position-time graph of a vehicle is a straight line parallel to the time axis at the 40 m mark from t = 0 s to t = 10 s. Seema reads it as 'moving at 40 m/s'. What should she conclude?
questions.a: The vehicle is at rest, 40 m from the origin. The position stays at 40 m, so the slope and the velocity are zero; the vehicle is at rest at 40 m from the origin.
o: The vehicle is at rest, 40 m from the origin
The vehicle moves at a constant velocity of 40 m/s
The vehicle moves with a constant acceleration of 4 m/s^2
The vehicle has travelled a distance of 400 m

questions.q: A velocity-time graph of a car is a straight sloped line from (0 s, 4 m/s) to (10 s, 24 m/s). What is the displacement of the car in these 10 s?
questions.a: 140 m, the area under the line. The area is a rectangle 4 x 10 = 40 m plus a triangle (1/2) x 10 x 20 = 100 m, which is 140 m.
o: 140 m, the area under the line
240 m, from the final velocity and the time
40 m, from the initial velocity and the time
20 m, from the slope alone

questions.q: The positions of a vehicle at 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 s are 0, 2, 8, 18 and 32 m. A student plots them and joins the points. Which statement describes the graph and the motion?
questions.a: A curve, because the displacement grows in each successive second (2, 6, 10, 14 m) and the velocity is increasing. Unequal displacements in equal intervals mean the velocity is changing, so the graph is a curve; the curve does not show the road's shape.
o: A curve, because the displacement grows in each successive second (2, 6, 10, 14 m) and the velocity is increasing
A straight line, because every point has a larger position than the one before
A curve, because the vehicle is moving along a curved road
A straight line, because the vehicle is at rest at each reading

questions.q: Which statement about graphs of motion in a straight line is false?
questions.a: The area enclosed between a position-time graph and the time axis gives the displacement. The area belongs to the velocity-time graph; the position-time graph gives velocity through its slope.
o: The area enclosed between a position-time graph and the time axis gives the displacement
The slope of a position-time graph gives the average velocity
The slope of a velocity-time graph gives the acceleration
The area between a velocity-time graph and the time axis gives the displacement

questions.q:
Study these statements about graphs of straight-line motion.
Statement 1: On a position-time graph, a line parallel to the time axis shows an object moving with a constant non-zero velocity.
Statement 2: A straight sloped line on a velocity-time graph shows constant acceleration, which equals its slope.
Statement 3: A curved position-time graph shows the actual curved route the object followed on the ground.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 2 only. Statement 1 is false: the object is at rest. Statement 3 is false: a graph is not a route map. Statement 2 is correct.
o: 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 only
1, 2 and 3

questions.q:
Assertion (A): On a velocity-time graph, a straight line parallel to the time axis means the acceleration is zero.
Reason (R): The slope of a velocity-time graph gives the acceleration, and a line parallel to the time axis has zero slope.
questions.a: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A. Both are true, and the zero slope is exactly why the acceleration is zero.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q: On a velocity-time graph a car's line runs straight from 0 m/s at 0 s to 12 m/s at 6 s. The area under the line for these 6 s, in metres, is ___.

Match each graph described in column I with what it shows in column II.
Column I: 1. A position-time straight line through the origin and (5 s, 30 m)  2. A position-time line parallel to the time axis at 18 m  3. A velocity-time line parallel to the time axis at 6 m/s from 0 s to 10 s, with the area under it  4. A velocity-time straight line from the origin to (10 s, 20 m/s), with its slope
Column II: a. velocity 6 m/s  b. the object at rest 18 m from the origin  c. acceleration 2 m/s^2  d. displacement 60 m
questions.a: 1-a, 2-b, 3-d, 4-c. 30/5 = 6 m/s from the slope; a flat position-time line is rest; 6 x 10 = 60 m from the area; 20/10 = 2 m/s^2 from the slope.

questions.q:
A student records time (s): 0, 3, 6, 9 and position (m): 0, 6, 12, 18.
(a) What shape will the position-time graph have? Give the reason from the data.
(b) Find the slope and say what it represents.
questions.a: (a) A straight line, since the displacement is the same (6 m) in every 3 s interval, so the velocity is constant. (b) Slope = 18/9 = 2 m/s, the average velocity.
s: Part (a): straight line, equal displacements in equal times
Part (b): slope 2 m/s as the velocity

questions.q:
A velocity-time graph of a braking car is a straight line from (0 s, 20 m/s) down to (5 s, 0 m/s).
(a) Find the acceleration from the slope.
(b) Find the displacement in the 5 s from the area.
questions.a: (a) Slope = (0 - 20)/5 = -4 m/s^2. (b) Area of the triangle = (1/2) x 5 x 20 = 50 m.

questions.q: True or False: A curved position-time graph means that the object is travelling along a curved road. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. A curved position-time graph means the velocity is changing (accelerated motion); a graph is not a route map and says nothing about the shape of the path.
s: Reason: the curve shows position changing unevenly with time; the path may be straight

questions.q: A graph paper scale is X-axis: 5 divisions = 1 s and Y-axis: 5 divisions = 20 m. How many divisions along each axis will you count to plot the point (3.5 s, 60 m)? Show the working.
questions.a: X: 3.5 s x 5 divisions per second = 17.5 divisions. Y: 60 m / 20 m x 5 divisions = 15 divisions.

questions.q: On one position-time graph, the line for B is steeper than the line for A. Raj says B is ahead of A. Is he right? Explain what the steeper line shows.
questions.a: Not necessarily. A steeper position-time line means a larger velocity (more displacement in the same time interval), not a larger position; B can start behind A.
s: Steeper line shows greater velocity, not greater position

questions.q: Sunita claims: 'A line parallel to the time axis on a velocity-time graph means the object is at rest.' Test the claim with a line at 6 m/s from 0 to 10 s.
questions.a: The claim is not correct. A line parallel to the time axis on a velocity-time graph means constant velocity and zero acceleration. At 6 m/s the object moves, and covers 6 x 10 = 60 m, the area under the line. Rest would need the line on the time axis (0 m/s).
s: Moves 60 m at 6 m/s, so not at rest

questions.q: A velocity-time graph of a car is a straight line from (4 s, 6 m/s) to (12 s, 18 m/s). Find (i) its acceleration, (ii) its displacement between 4 s and 12 s using a rectangle and a triangle, and (iii) the quantity you get if you divide the displacement by 8 s.
questions.a: (i) Slope = (18 - 6)/(12 - 4) = 1.5 m/s^2. (ii) Rectangle 6 x 8 = 48 m plus triangle (1/2) x 8 x 12 = 48 m gives 96 m. (iii) 96/8 = 12 m/s, the average velocity.
s: Displacement 96 m from rectangle plus triangle

questions.q: Describe a velocity-time graph, with its numbers, for a straight line from 0 s to 6 s that encloses an area of 90 m with the time axis. Show that the area works out.
questions.a: Example: a line parallel to the time axis at 15 m/s from 0 s to 6 s: area = 15 x 6 = 90 m. (Another: a straight line from 0 m/s at 0 s to 30 m/s at 6 s: (1/2) x 6 x 30 = 90 m.)

questions.q:
The velocity-time graph of a cyclist on a straight road has three parts: a straight line from 0 m/s at 0 s to 6 m/s at 10 s; a line parallel to the time axis at 6 m/s from 10 s to 40 s; and a straight line from 6 m/s at 40 s down to 0 m/s at 50 s.
(i) Find the acceleration in each part.
(ii) Find the displacement in each part from the area.
(iii) Find the total displacement.
(iv) Find the average velocity for the 50 s.
(v) The cyclist's average acceleration over the 50 s is zero although the accelerations in parts one and three are not zero. Explain.
questions.a: (i) 0.6 m/s^2, 0 and -0.6 m/s^2. (ii) (1/2) x 10 x 6 = 30 m; 6 x 30 = 180 m; (1/2) x 10 x 6 = 30 m. (iii) 240 m. (iv) 240/50 = 4.8 m/s. (v) The velocity is 0 at the start and at the end, so the change in velocity over the 50 s is zero; the speeding-up (+0.6) and slowing-down (-0.6) cancel in the average.
s: Zero change in velocity gives zero average acceleration

questions.q:
A vehicle starting from rest has these positions: 0 m at 0 s, 3 m at 2 s, 12 m at 4 s, 27 m at 6 s and 48 m at 8 s.
(i) Find the displacement in each 2 s interval.
(ii) Find the average velocity in each interval.
(iii) Say whether the position-time graph is a straight line or a curve, with the reason.
(iv) By how much does the average velocity rise from one interval to the next, and what does it show about the acceleration?
(v) A student draws one straight line from the first point to the last. Find the average velocity this line gives and say why it misleads.
questions.a: (i) 3, 9, 15 and 21 m. (ii) 1.5, 4.5, 7.5 and 10.5 m/s. (iii) A curve, because equal time intervals give unequal (increasing) displacements. (iv) It rises by 3 m/s every 2 s, so the acceleration is constant at about 1.5 m/s^2. (v) 48/8 = 6 m/s; it hides that the vehicle was slow at first (1.5 m/s) and fast later (10.5 m/s).
s: Rise of 3 m/s per 2 s means constant acceleration
Straight line gives 6 m/s and misleads

questions.q:
Two runners start together on a straight 150 m track. On a position-time graph, runner A's line is straight from the origin to (10 s, 50 m), and runner B's line is straight from (0 s, 20 m) to (10 s, 60 m), because B was given a head start. Both keep their velocity.
(a) Find the velocity of each runner from the slopes.
(b) After how many seconds does A catch B?
(c) In a 150 m race with these head start and velocities, who wins and by how much time?
(d) The coach wants a fair race. What head start would make them finish together, and is it sensible to give it?
questions.a: (a) A: 50/10 = 5 m/s; B: (60 - 20)/10 = 4 m/s. (b) 5t = 20 + 4t gives t = 20 s (at 100 m). (c) A takes 150/5 = 30 s; B has 130 m to go at 4 m/s = 32.5 s; A wins by 2.5 s. (d) A head start h with (150 - h)/4 = 30 gives h = 30 m. A reasoned view is accepted: it makes the race tie, but A then has no chance of winning and a tie decides nothing.
s: Part (d): 30 m with a justified view

questions.q:
A lift in a mall climbs 20 m. Its velocity-time graph has three parts: a straight line from 0 m/s at 0 s to 2 m/s at 4 s, a line parallel to the time axis at 2 m/s from 4 s to 10 s, and a straight line from 2 m/s at 10 s down to 0 m/s at 14 s.
(a) Find the acceleration in the first part.
(b) Find the acceleration in the third part, with its direction relative to the velocity.
(c) Show from the graph that the lift climbs 20 m.
(d) The owner wants a faster trip of the same 20 m. Option 1: keep both 4 s speeding-up and slowing-down parts but raise the cruise velocity to 2.5 m/s. Find the new total time and the new acceleration in the first part, and say whether you would accept the change.
questions.a: (a) 2/4 = 0.5 m/s^2. (b) (0 - 2)/4 = -0.5 m/s^2, opposite to the velocity. (c) Area = (1/2) x 4 x 2 + 2 x 6 + (1/2) x 4 x 2 = 4 + 12 + 4 = 20 m. (d) The two ramps cover (1/2) x 4 x 2.5 x 2 = 10 m, so the cruise covers 10 m at 2.5 m/s = 4 s; total = 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 s (2 s saved). The first-part acceleration becomes 2.5/4 = 0.625 m/s^2, 25 percent more. A reasoned view is accepted: 2 s saved against a stronger push on riders.
s: Part (d): 12 s and 0.625 m/s^2 with a justified decision

questions.q: A cyclist moving at 4 m/s along a straight road speeds up at a constant 0.5 m/s^2 for 10 s. Which value is the distance she covers in these 10 s?
questions.a: 65 m. s = ut + (1/2)at^2 = 4 x 10 + (1/2)(0.5)(100) = 40 + 25 = 65 m; 90 m forgets the half, 25 m drops the ut term, and 42.5 m forgets to square t.

questions.q: A car braking at a constant 5 m/s^2 needs 62.5 m to stop from 25 m/s. At half the speed (12.5 m/s) with the same braking, what stopping distance should the driver expect?
questions.a: About 15.6 m, one quarter of 62.5 m. From v^2 = u^2 + 2as with v = 0, s = u^2/(2|a|); halving u divides u^2 by 4, so s = 156.25/10 = 15.6 m.
o: About 15.6 m, one quarter of 62.5 m
About 31.3 m, half of 62.5 m
About 62.5 m, because the braking is the same
About 125 m, because slower cars take longer

questions.q: A train passes a signal at 20 m/s and slows uniformly to 10 m/s over the next 150 m. Which value is its constant acceleration?
questions.a: -1 m/s^2. No time is given, so use v^2 = u^2 + 2as: 100 = 400 + 2a(150), giving a = -300/300 = -1 m/s^2.

questions.q: To find the braking distance of a car moving at 30 m/s, Veena puts a = +5 m/s^2 in v^2 = u^2 + 2as with v = 0 and gets s = -90 m. What is her slip?
questions.a: She gave the braking acceleration the wrong sign; it is -5 m/s^2 and the distance is 90 m. Braking acceleration opposes the velocity, so with the motion positive a = -5 m/s^2; then 0 = 900 - 10s gives s = 90 m.
o: She gave the braking acceleration the wrong sign; it is -5 m/s^2 and the distance is 90 m
She should have used v = u + at, which gives the same distance
She used the right sign and the car really moves backwards
She should have used u = 0 for a car that is braking

questions.q: In which situation are the three kinematic equations of this chapter not valid?
questions.a: A car whose acceleration keeps increasing as it speeds up. The equations hold only when the acceleration is constant; the other three situations have constant acceleration.
o: A car whose acceleration keeps increasing as it speeds up
A stone falling freely near the ground
A train braking at a steady rate in a straight line
A bike speeding up by equal amounts in equal times

questions.q:
Read these statements about the kinematic equations.
Statement 1: The equation v^2 = u^2 + 2as can give a stopping distance without knowing the time.
Statement 2: In straight-line motion in both directions, the signs of u, v, a and s tell their directions.
Statement 3: If the initial speed of a braking car is doubled with the same braking, the stopping distance also only doubles.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 1 and 2 only. Statement 3 is false: s = u^2/(2|a|), so doubling u makes the stopping distance four times as large.
o: 1 and 2 only
2 only
1, 2 and 3
2 and 3 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A car braking from 20 m/s at -2.5 m/s^2 travels 80 m before stopping.
Reason (R): The car takes 8 s to stop.
questions.a: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A. A is true since s = 400/5 = 80 m. R is also true (t = 20/2.5 = 8 s), but the stopping time is a separate result from the same data; it does not give the distance 80 m.
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.q: A car starts from rest and moves with a constant acceleration of 3 m/s^2. The distance it covers in 4 s is ___ m.

Match each situation (column I) with the quantity that the kinematic equations give (column II).
Column I: 1. A scooter at 5 m/s with an acceleration of 2 m/s^2 for 3 s: final velocity  2. A car from rest at 2 m/s^2 for 5 s: distance covered  3. A vehicle from rest reaching 12 m/s with a = 3 m/s^2: distance covered  4. A vehicle at 20 m/s braking at -5 m/s^2 until it stops: distance covered
Column II: a. 11 m/s  b. 25 m  c. 24 m  d. 40 m

A truck moving at 12 m/s speeds up at a constant 1.5 m/s^2 for 8 s on a straight road.
(a) Find its final velocity.
(b) Find the distance it covers in these 8 s.

A motorbike moving at 24 m/s stops, with a constant acceleration, after travelling 72 m.
(a) Find its acceleration.
(b) Use it to find the time taken to stop.
s: Part (b): 6 s using the acceleration from (a)

questions.q: True or False: A stone dropped from rest falls four times as far in 2 s as it does in the first 1 s. Give a reason.
questions.a: True. With u = 0 and a = g = 9.8 m/s^2, s = (1/2)gt^2 is 4.9 m at 1 s and 19.6 m at 2 s, which is four times as far.
s: Reason: s = (1/2)gt^2 depends on t squared, and 2 squared is 4

questions.q: Ravi applies v = u + at to a car whose acceleration keeps growing as the driver presses harder on the accelerator. Is his method valid? Give the reason.
questions.a: No. The kinematic equations are valid only when the acceleration is constant; here the acceleration changes with time, so the equation would give an incorrect velocity.

questions.q: A goods train moving at 20 m/s brakes with a constant acceleration of -0.5 m/s^2 until it stops. Name the equation that gives the stopping distance directly and find the distance.
questions.a: Use v^2 = u^2 + 2as, since the time is not given. With v = 0, 0 = 400 + 2(-0.5)s, so s = 400 m.
s: v^2 = u^2 + 2as chosen because time is not given

questions.q: Pooja claims: 'A car moving at 30 m/s and braking at 4 m/s^2 (an acceleration of -4 m/s^2) travels 112.5 m before it comes to rest.' Test her claim.
questions.a: The claim is correct. With v = 0, v^2 = u^2 + 2as gives 0 = 900 + 2(-4)s, so s = 900/8 = 112.5 m.

questions.q: A scooter moving at 10 m/s brakes at a constant -2 m/s^2. Show that it cannot travel 30 m before slowing to a stop and give the stopping distance.
questions.a: Putting v = 0, u = 10 and a = -2 in v^2 = u^2 + 2as gives s = 100/4 = 25 m. The scooter has stopped after 25 m, so it cannot travel 30 m; substituting s = 30 would give v^2 = 100 - 120, a negative number, which is impossible.
s: Cannot reach 30 m since it stops
Check: v^2 would be negative for s = 30

questions.q: A ball is dropped from a bridge and takes 3 s to hit the river below. Take g = 9.8 m/s^2 and neglect air. Find (i) the height of the bridge above the river, (ii) the ball's velocity as it hits, and (iii) a check of (ii) using v^2 = u^2 + 2as.

A scooter moving at 54 km/h sees an obstacle 40 m ahead. The rider takes 0.6 s to react before braking. Once the brakes are applied the scooter slows with a constant acceleration of -4 m/s^2.
(i) Convert the speed to m/s.
(ii) Find the distance covered during the reaction time.
(iii) Find the braking distance.
(iv) Will the scooter stop before the obstacle? State the margin.
(v) If the reaction time were 0.8 s instead, would the result change? Show it.
questions.a: (i) 54 km/h = 15 m/s. (ii) 15 x 0.6 = 9 m. (iii) 0 = 225 + 2(-4)s gives s = 28.125 m. (iv) Total = 37.125 m, which is less than 40 m, so it stops 2.875 m short of the obstacle. (v) Yes: 15 x 0.8 = 12 m, total 40.125 m, which is more than 40 m, so it would reach the obstacle.
s: 0.8 s gives 40.125 m and the scooter hits the obstacle

questions.q:
A car brakes with a constant acceleration of -5 m/s^2 from 36 km/h in one case and from 72 km/h in another.
(i) Find the stopping distance in each case.
(ii) Find the stopping time in each case.
(iii) Compare the ratios of the speeds, the distances and the times.
(iv) A driver at 72 km/h keeps a gap of 20 m from a stationary vehicle, ignoring reaction time. Does he stop in time?
(v) What is the highest speed, to the nearest km/h, from which he could stop within 20 m?
questions.a: (i) 10 m/s: 100/10 = 10 m; 20 m/s: 400/10 = 40 m. (ii) 10/5 = 2 s and 20/5 = 4 s. (iii) Speed ratio 2, time ratio 2, distance ratio 4. (iv) No: he needs 40 m, more than the 20 m gap. (v) v^2 = 2 x 5 x 20 = 200, v = 14.14 m/s, about 51 km/h.

questions.q:
On an expressway, a car follows a truck at 20 m/s, both in a straight line. The truck brakes suddenly with an acceleration of -5 m/s^2. The car driver reacts after 1 s, during which the car keeps its speed, and then brakes with -4 m/s^2. Both stop completely.
(a) Find the distance the truck covers from the start of its braking until it stops.
(b) Find the total distance the car covers from the truck's first braking until the car stops.
(c) Find the smallest initial gap between the two vehicles that avoids a collision.
(d) The authority must advise a following gap in seconds at 20 m/s. Compare a 1.5 s and a 2 s gap using your result, and recommend one with a stated drawback.
questions.a: (a) 400/(2 x 5) = 40 m. (b) 20 m in the reaction second plus 400/(2 x 4) = 50 m, total 70 m. (c) 70 - 40 = 30 m. (d) A 1.5 s gap at 20 m/s is 30 m, exactly the minimum with no margin; a 2 s gap is 40 m, with a 10 m margin. A reasoned choice is accepted: 2 s is safer but takes more road space per vehicle; 1.5 s allows more vehicles but leaves no room for a slower reaction.
s: Part (d): compares 30 m and 40 m gaps with a justified recommendation

questions.q:
A village group wants to know the depth of an open well. A boy drops a stone from rest and times it to the water with a stopwatch: 2.4 s. The stopwatch could be off by 0.2 s either way. Take g = 9.8 m/s^2 and ignore air and the time for sound. The group plans to line the well if it is deeper than 30 m.
(a) Find the depth from the 2.4 s reading.
(b) Find the velocity with which the stone hits the water.
(c) Find the least and the greatest depths that the 2.2 s and 2.6 s readings allow.
(d) Should the group order lining for a well deeper than 30 m, given the range? Decide and say what you give up.
questions.a: (a) (1/2)(9.8)(2.4^2) = 28.2 m. (b) 9.8 x 2.4 = 23.5 m/s. (c) 2.2 s gives 23.7 m and 2.6 s gives 33.1 m. (d) The range spans 30 m. A reasoned choice is accepted: ordering lining protects against the deeper case but may waste money if the well is 24 m; waiting and re-timing costs time but removes the doubt.
s: Part (d): a decision with its trade-off

questions.q: A child on a park roundabout of radius 7 m takes 22 s for one full revolution. Taking pi = 22/7, which row gives the distance travelled, the average speed and the average velocity for one revolution?
questions.a: 44 m, 2 m/s and 0 m/s. Distance = 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 m, so speed = 44/22 = 2 m/s; she ends where she began, so the displacement and average velocity are zero.
o: 44 m, 2 m/s and 0 m/s
44 m, 2 m/s and 2 m/s
22 m, 1 m/s and 0 m/s
0 m, 0 m/s and 0 m/s

questions.q: The tip of a clock's minute hand of length 7 cm moves for exactly 3 hours. Taking pi = 22/7, which pair gives the distance travelled by the tip and its displacement?
questions.a: 132 cm and 0 cm. The minute hand makes 3 complete revolutions, each 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 cm, so the distance is 132 cm; the tip is back at its starting position, so the displacement is zero.
o: 132 cm and 0 cm
44 cm and 0 cm
132 cm and 132 cm
0 cm and 132 cm

questions.q: A marble goes round the inside of a tape ring lying on a smooth table. At the instant it is at the easternmost point of the ring, moving north, the ring is lifted without touching the marble. What does it do next?
questions.a: It moves north in a straight line, along the tangent at that point. The marble continues in the direction of its velocity at the instant of release, which is along the tangent; at the easternmost point the tangent points north.
o: It moves north in a straight line, along the tangent at that point
It moves west in a straight line, towards the centre of the ring
It keeps moving round in the same circle
It moves east in a straight line, away from the centre

questions.q: One athlete runs at a steady speed round a regular hexagonal track and another, at the same speed, round a regular 12-sided track. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The second changes direction 12 times a round, and as the sides increase the track tends to a circle with continuous change of direction. The number of turns per round equals the number of sides (6 and 12); as it grows the turns become more frequent until the direction of the velocity changes continuously on a circle.
o: The second changes direction 12 times a round, and as the sides increase the track tends to a circle with continuous change of direction
Both change direction the same number of times, since the speed is the same
The first changes direction more often because its sides are longer
Neither changes direction, since the speed does not change

questions.q: Which statement about uniform circular motion is not correct?
questions.a: The acceleration is zero, because the speed does not change. The direction of the velocity keeps changing, so the motion is accelerated even though the speed is constant.
o: The acceleration is zero, because the speed does not change
The speed is the same at every point of the circle
The velocity at any point is along the tangent to the circle
The displacement after one full revolution is zero

questions.q:
Read these statements about uniform circular motion.
Statement 1: The velocity at any point of the circle is directed towards the centre of the circle.
Statement 2: The average velocity over one full revolution is 2 pi R / T.
Statement 3: The speed is the same at every point and only the direction of the velocity changes.
Which statements are correct?
questions.a: 3 only. Statement 1 is false because the velocity is along the tangent. Statement 2 is false because 2 pi R / T is the average speed; the average velocity is zero. Statement 3 is correct.
o: 3 only
1 only
1 and 3 only
2 only

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The displacement of a child on a merry-go-round after one full revolution is zero.
Reason (R): In one revolution the displacement equals the circumference of the circle.
questions.a: A is true but R is false. A is true since the child returns to the starting position. R is false: the circumference is the distance travelled in one revolution.
o: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true

questions.q: A cyclist rides at constant speed round a circular track of radius 21 m and takes 33 s for one lap. Taking pi = 22/7, her average speed is ___ m/s.

Match each item about a circular track of radius 7 m (pi = 22/7) with its value or direction.
Column I: 1. Distance in one revolution  2. Displacement after 5 complete revolutions  3. Average speed of a body that takes 11 s for one revolution  4. Direction of the velocity of a body at a point P of the circle
Column II: a. 44 m  b. 0 m  c. 4 m/s  d. along the tangent at P
