questions.a: 1-a, 2-b, 3-c, 4-d. 2 x (22/7) x 7 = 44 m; the body is back at its start after complete revolutions; 44/11 = 4 m/s; velocity is along the tangent.

questions.q:
A toy car goes round a circular track of radius 14 m, taking 22 s for each lap (pi = 22/7).
(a) Find the distance it travels in one lap.
(b) Find its average speed and its average velocity for the lap.
questions.a: (a) 2 x (22/7) x 14 = 88 m. (b) Average speed = 88/22 = 4 m/s; the displacement is zero, so the average velocity is 0 m/s.

questions.q:
An athlete runs round a regular octagonal track at a steady speed.
(a) How many times does the direction of her velocity change in one round?
(b) What happens to this number as the number of sides is increased indefinitely, and what does the track become?
questions.a: (a) Eight times, once at each corner. (b) The turns come more and more often, the track tends to a circle, and the direction of the velocity changes continuously.
s: Part (b): tends to continuous change on a circle

questions.q: True or False: A body in uniform circular motion has zero acceleration because its speed does not change. Give a reason.
questions.a: False. Acceleration is non-zero whenever the velocity changes in magnitude or direction or both; in uniform circular motion the direction of the velocity changes continuously, so the motion is accelerated.
s: Reason: velocity has a direction, and it keeps changing even when the speed is constant

questions.q: Ananya says, 'A runner who finishes one lap of a circular track in time T has an average velocity of 2 pi R / T.' Is she correct? Correct her if needed.
questions.a: No. 2 pi R / T is the average speed, since 2 pi R is the distance in one lap. The displacement is zero after one lap, so the average velocity is zero.
s: Identifies 2 pi R / T as the average speed
States average velocity is 0 since the displacement is 0

questions.q: A driver says, 'My car is not accelerating; the speedometer shows a steady 40 km/h as I go round the roundabout.' Respond using this chapter.
questions.a: The car is accelerating. The speedometer shows only the magnitude of the velocity; on the circular path the direction of the velocity changes continuously, so the velocity changes and the acceleration is not zero.
s: The steady reading shows only a constant speed
The changing direction means the motion is accelerated

questions.q: Dev claims: 'In uniform circular motion both the speed and the velocity of the body are constant.' Test the claim.
questions.a: The claim is partly right. The speed is constant, the same at every point of the circle. The velocity is not constant, because its direction (along the tangent) keeps changing, so the motion is accelerated.

questions.q: Show that for a body in uniform circular motion, the average velocity over one full revolution can never be equal to the average speed.
questions.a: Average speed = 2 pi R / T, which is not zero because the distance is the circumference. After a full revolution the displacement is zero, so average velocity = 0/T = 0. A non-zero value cannot equal zero, so the two are never equal.
s: Average speed 2 pi R / T, non-zero
Displacement zero, so average velocity zero

questions.q: A car goes round a circular roundabout of radius 21 m at a constant speed, completing each lap in 33 s (pi = 22/7). It makes 5 laps. Find (i) the total distance, (ii) the total time, (iii) the displacement after the 5 laps.
questions.a: (i) One lap is 2 x (22/7) x 21 = 132 m, so 5 laps = 660 m. (ii) 5 x 33 = 165 s. (iii) The car is back at its starting point, so the displacement is zero.

questions.q:
A Ferris wheel of radius 14 m turns anticlockwise at a constant speed and takes 44 s for one revolution (pi = 22/7). A rider takes a ride of 5 revolutions.
(i) Find the distance moved in one revolution.
(ii) Find the rider's speed.
(iii) Find the distance and the displacement for the whole ride.
(iv) Give the directions of the velocity at the highest and the lowest points.
(v) Is the motion accelerated? Use (iv) to explain.
questions.a: (i) 88 m. (ii) 88/44 = 2 m/s. (iii) 5 x 88 = 440 m; displacement 0. (iv) At the highest point the velocity is horizontal and to the left; at the lowest point it is horizontal and to the right. (v) Yes: the speed is the same at both points but the two velocities are in opposite directions, so the velocity changes and the motion is accelerated.
s: Opposite directions along the tangents at top and bottom

questions.q:
Two friends run one lap each on concentric circular tracks of radii 7 m and 14 m (pi = 22/7). Each takes 22 s per lap at a constant speed.
(i) Find the distance each runs in a lap.
(ii) Find the average speed of each.
(iii) Find the average velocity of each over a lap.
(iv) One friend says, 'We took the same time, so our speeds are equal.' Evaluate the statement.
(v) Is either runner's motion unaccelerated? Give a reason.
questions.a: (i) 44 m and 88 m. (ii) 2 m/s and 4 m/s. (iii) Zero for both, as each returns to the start. (iv) Not correct: equal times with different distances give different speeds, 2 m/s against 4 m/s. (v) No: both change the direction of the velocity continuously, so both are accelerated.
s: Statement rejected with the distances as the reason
Both accelerated through the changing direction

questions.q:
A fair has two designs of a circular ride, and a rider is on the ride for 180 s in each. Design A has radius 7 m and takes 20 s per revolution. Design B has radius 3.5 m and takes 10 s per revolution. Use pi = 22/7 and assume a constant speed.
(a) Find the distance a rider covers in 180 s on Design A.
(b) Find the speed on each design and the distance covered on Design B.
(c) Find the number of revolutions made on each design and the displacement after the ride.
(d) The owner must choose one design. State which you would choose, using your results, and one thing you give up.
questions.a: (a) Circumference 44 m, 9 revolutions: 396 m. (b) A: 44/20 = 2.2 m/s; B: 22/10 = 2.2 m/s, so distance 2.2 x 180 = 396 m. (c) A: 9 revolutions; B: 18 revolutions; the displacement is zero on both, since each ends at the start. (d) The speed and distance are equal, so the choice rests on other things. A reasoned choice is accepted: B needs a smaller space but the direction of the rider's velocity changes twice as often; A has gentler turning but needs the larger area.
s: Part (b): 2.2 m/s for both and 396 m
Part (d): a justified choice with a trade-off

questions.q:
A school ground has a regular hexagonal training track with each side 20 m. A runner runs it at a steady 4 m/s and runs 3 rounds. The coach is thinking of changing it to a circular track of the same perimeter, hoping to remove the sudden direction changes at the corners.
(a) How long does one round take?
(b) How many times does the direction of her velocity change during the 3 rounds?
(c) What are her displacement and average velocity after the 3 rounds?
(d) Will the circular track remove acceleration? Decide and give the reason, naming what does change.
questions.a: (a) Perimeter 6 x 20 = 120 m, time 120/4 = 30 s. (b) 6 turns per round, so 18 turns. (c) She is back at her start, so the displacement and average velocity are zero. (d) No. On the circle the direction of the velocity changes continuously, so the runner is still accelerated; what changes is that the turning is spread over the whole path instead of happening only at six corners.
s: Part (d): still accelerated, continuous change of direction
